notes:
Summary: Pallisade is evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for a factory-floor assistant and telemetry summarization pipeline. Primary ask: predictable throughput guarantees and strict latency SLOs for operator chat and alerting. They want dedicated GPU capacity (reserved) with fallbacks to hosted during maintenance windows.

Workload profile: mostly short interactive chat (operator queries, status checks) and periodic batch summarization of telemetry windows. Peak concurrency expected 350-500 concurrent operator sessions during daytime shift; baseline 60-100 overnight. Avg response length 40-120 tokens; some long summaries up to 4k tokens.

SLO & throughput targets (asked on call):
- P95 latency <= 200ms for short chat responses (<= 128 tokens).
- P99 tail latency target <= 350-400ms; they want wording in SLA about p99 and sustained load handling.
- Sustained throughput goal: 400 reqs/s steady-state with 1.2k reqs/s burst for 30s windows.

Reserved GPU planning notes:
- Initial estimate: 4-6 H100-class slots for baseline; plan for 8 slots for burst headroom. They asked for modeling of token/sec economics across 4/8/16 GPU commitments.
- Want explicit guidance on autoscaling/burst capacity policies and transparent preemption behavior when committed capacity is exhausted.

Model-specific tuning requirements discussed:
- Context length: 32k for telemetry summarization POC; need guidance on memory vs throughput tradeoffs and recommended kernel profiles.
- Quantization profiles: Will try 4-bit quant for large model variants; ask for Redwood's recommended quant profiles and fallback variants (int8 / fp16) for latency-sensitive routes.
- Batching & KV cache: Close coordination with their inference engineers. They prefer small, latency-minded batching (batch size 8-16 for interactive) and aggressive KV caching for long-context sessions to avoid re-encoding prefixes. Need POC configs to test cache hit rates and how cache invalidation ties into their session model.

Security / compliance: Must run in customer VPC for PII telemetry. Require KMS-integrated keys in Private deployment and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. Data residency restriction: US only.

Commercial / SLA negotiation points:
- They want explicit credits if p99 latency exceeds agreed threshold across monthly rolling windows.
- Request a 12-month committed tier with breakpoints at 6/12 months for additional GPU add-ons.
- Need a clear escalation path and runbook for failover to Redwood hosted catalog models in case of private capacity outage.

- 2026-01-12: Intro + requirements call (Fireflies ff_call_2026_01_12_873).
- 2026-02-05: Architecture deep-dive with infra and security teams; provided preliminary network diagrams.

- 2026-03-09: Internal Redwood prep: generate GPU commitment cost model and draft SLA language for CX review.

POC milestones for evaluation:
- Perf bench (week 1): validate p95/p99 under synthetic traces matching operator load.
- Model tuning (week 2-3): test 32k context, verify KV cache hit improvement, iterate quant profiles.
- Live pilot (week 4-6): run on two factory sites in PRD-like network; measure SLOs and operational playbooks.

Customer quotes / call snippets: "If we can't get consistent p99 under 400ms our operators won't adopt it."; "Need a clear cost model that shows us break-even vs. self-hosting at 12 months."

Next steps (short): finalize dedicated sizing recommendation, deliver SLA draft, schedule POC kickoff for 2026-04-15, confirm billing/account team for committed contract.
